correctness.rationale: At \(n=6\), the law \(\operatorname{Bin}(6,1/2)\) is symmetric about three, so all three left-loadedness coefficients vanish. For \(n>6\), Simmons' binomial inequality gives \(\alpha_1>0\). Putting \(x=n-3\ge4\), fresh algebra confirms \(\Pr(X=6)/\Pr(X=0)-1=(x-3)Q(x)/(80x^5)\) with \(Q(x)=x^4+246x^3+333x^2-216x-324\), and \(Q(x)=x^4+246x^3+333(x-4)^2+2448(x-4)+4140>0\). Hence \(\Pr(X=6)>\Pr(X=0)\), so \(\alpha_3<0\). With only \(\alpha_2\) between these endpoint coefficients, either sign of \(\alpha_2\) produces exactly the \(L_1\) single-sign-change condition. This proves every integer \(n\ge6\), not merely a finite test range.
residual_risks: The proof is special to mean three because only one coefficient lies between the two forced endpoint signs.
